branch_policy: LONG-LIVED: no per-phase branches; every phase commits here
WHY_NO_ENGINEERS: This SRD's §12 is a HOST RUNBOOK, not a code plan, so no engineer was dispatched. Verified 2026-09-12: (a) the provider design is already implemented -- src/config/schema.ts carries the full provider block and `providers` flows through 12 source files -- and already tested across 17 provider test files, with every §10 probe spot-checked present; (b) ISA.md has ZERO open `[ ]` criteria (963/990, 27 partial, 6 retired); (c) the only config phase edits fleet.yaml, which is .gitignore:9 and untracked, so no branch, PR, CI run or merge can carry it. Dispatching subagents here would have been theatre. The repo work that DOES exist is correcting this SRD from live measurement, which is what the branch carries.

findings: --kv-cache-dtype fp8 is live and was absent from every draft of §6.9.2. Not NVFP4-specific; must be KEPT through the swap.

phases.name: Fetch bf16 weights
phases.completion_evidence: model-00001-of-00002.safetensors 49907246508 bytes + model-00002-of-00002.safetensors 1704763408 bytes = 51612009916, against the index's 51611872412 tensor-byte total (the ~137KB excess is safetensors header framing). Zero .incomplete files. Container running=false exit=0 -- the first poll at which that exit code meant anything, since it is the unset default while a container lives.
phases.instrumentation_lesson: du -sh ROUNDED to the same figure on consecutive polls (false 'progress'); du -sb reported ALLOCATED BLOCKS and plateaued while the sparse shard was written (false 'stall'); stat reported the write offset and also plateaued because hf writes via parallel range requests. The only honest signals were the container's network counter and the terminal state. I nearly reported a stall on two of these.
phases.mechanism: detached container `gemma4-bf16-dl` from vllm/vllm-openai:latest, which already ships hf 1.19.0 -- chosen so gabe's system Python is never mutated (no hf/huggingface-cli/uv installed on the host)
phases.rollback: the NVFP4 directory is UNTOUCHED and is the rollback

phases.name: Reconfigure (PRODUCTION RESTART)
phases.verification: Key enforcement proven THREE ways: no key -> 401, wrong key -> 401, correct key -> 200. That same call returned 200 to anyone before this phase. All three aliases served including gemma-4-e4b-it-mxfp8. bf16 genuinely generates (HTTP 200, finish_reason stop, correct output). LightRAG reaches rag-llm by name over ragnet using the key it already held: 200 with, 401 without. rag-llm resolves to 172.19.0.2 from inside lightrag. No OOM, restarts=0.
phases.memory_evidence: Dropping rag-embeddings 0.25 -> 0.08 reclaimed ~21GB (used 83 -> 62). Stopping rag-llm released a further ~44GB (used 62 -> 18). This confirms SRD 6.9.2's thesis that vLLM reserves gpu-memory-utilization x total irrespective of weight size -- a 4B embedding model was holding ~30GB.
phases.near_miss_worth_keeping: vLLM logged 'checkpoint size (48.07 GiB) exceeds 90% of available RAM (48.25 GiB)' during load -- a 0.18 GiB margin. Available dipped to 16GB mid-load then recovered to 31GB once page cache was released. It did not OOM, but the margin was far thinner than the plan implied.
must_preserve: all three --served-model-name aliases incl. gemma-4-e4b-it-mxfp8 which LightRAG is configured against
docker network connect ragnet AFTER create

phases.name: Prove the gate (Q13/Q14)
phases.note: CAN REFUSE THE PROVIDER OUTRIGHT. Concurrent probe at --max-num-seqs 8; a serial probe is not evidence.
phases.q13_result: PASS. Eight concurrent tool calls at --max-num-seqs 8: 8/8 emitted tool_calls, 8/8 carried the correct city argument, wall 2.51s. They were GENUINELY BATCHED -- each individual request took ~2.45s, so serialized execution would have been ~19.6s. The two upstream defects that made 'under load' the operative phrase did not manifest. The serial probe was also clean (finish_reason tool_calls, get_weather, city=Paris) but the SRD is explicit that a serial probe is not evidence, so the concurrent run is what closes this.
phases.q14_result: ANSWERED. Steady-state serial decode 24.5 tok/s (765 completion tokens in 31.25s). Aggregate under 8-way concurrency 49 tok/s. Against SRD 6.9.1's cited 27.8 tok/s for a 30B-class MoE on this silicon, the NVFP4 -> bf16 swap costs little. It also vindicates refusing the dense 31B, which the bandwidth argument predicted would ceiling near 4 tok/s: this is roughly 6x that.

phases.name: Expose to LAN
phases.precondition_met: the --api-key landed in Phase 3 and was proven enforcing BEFORE this phase bound anything to the subnet
phases.plan_defect_found_and_corrected: 12 Phase 5 as written says REBIND from 127.0.0.1:8001 TO 192.168.86.199:8001. Phase 6 points the tunnel at http://127.0.0.1:8001. Executing Phase 5 literally would have deleted Phase 6's target. Published on BOTH host IPs instead -- strictly more restrictive than 0.0.0.0, since gabe's Wi-Fi .213 is deliberately excluded.
phases.verified_from: 192.168.86.49 -- a SEPARATE machine on the subnet, which is the only vantage point that tests the actual threat model. Testing from gabe itself would have proven nothing.
evidence: no key -> 401, wrong key -> 401, correct key -> 200, all three aliases served over the LAN
raw TCP: 8001 OPEN, 8002 CLOSED -- exposure scoped to exactly one port, not a blanket opening
iptables -t nat DOCKER chain carries exactly TWO DNAT rules, -d 127.0.0.1/32 and -d 192.168.86.199/32, both to 172.17.0.2:8000. The dual bind is real at the packet level and .213 is absent.
two docker-proxy processes, matching the two bindings
loopback still answers 401, so Phase 6's tunnel target survives
BEFORE measurement taken first: 8001 and 8002 both unreachable from the LAN, ufw inactive, INPUT policy ACCEPT -- so the change is attributable and no firewall could mask it
phases.false_alarm_recorded: My first LAN probe returned 000 on every check and looked like a failed bind. It was not: curl's 14-retry budget was spent during the 48GiB model reload, so it gave up before vLLM bound. Re-tested against a ready server, everything passed. Reporting that as a broken bind would have been wrong.

phases.name: Tunnel
phases.note: cloudflared was absent; outbound 7844 verified OPEN from gabe. Stops short of the DNS record, which needs Phase 0's dashboard action.
phases.config_src: local -- locally-managed with /etc/cloudflared/config.yml, chosen because `cloudflared tunnel login` needs a browser and cannot run headless. The tunnel was created through the API with the token instead, and the credentials file written directly.
phases.ingress: inference2.agileguy.ca -> http://127.0.0.1:8001, with a http_status:404 catch-all. This is why Phase 5 had to KEEP the loopback binding rather than replace it.
phases.WHY_THIS_PUBLISHES_NOTHING_YET: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN can create and manage tunnels but CANNOT write DNS -- re-verified live 2026-09-12, zones/{id}/dns_records returns code 10000 Authentication error. Without the inference2.agileguy.ca CNAME, the tunnel runs and the hostname resolves to nothing. The exposure is therefore gated behind a dashboard action only the operator can take, which is a genuine safety boundary rather than an obstacle.
phases.collision_check: inference2 verified UNCLAIMED across all 8 tunnels on the account before creation. Only inference -> inference.agileguy.ca exists, on a different tunnel (macbook.local). The memory note warns that collisions silently break live services, so this was re-checked live rather than trusted.
phases.operator_step_to_publish: In the Cloudflare dashboard, add a CNAME: inference2.agileguy.ca -> 79be1ed1-ad5b-487a-a935-dfdfea5ba979.cfargotunnel.com, proxied. Nothing else is needed -- the tunnel and ingress are already in place.
phases.security_note_at_publish_time: Once that record exists, the ONLY gate on this endpoint is the single shared value in GABE_API_KEY -- the same one OMLX_API_KEY carries -- by explicit operator decision on 2026-09-12 after being offered a two-key alternative. SRD 9.2/7 records that the LAN accepted-risk argument -- 'an attacker is already adjacent to a port they can open anyway' -- is FALSE for a publicly-resolvable endpoint. The value is deliberately NOT written here: fleet.yaml is gitignored so operator credentials and endpoints stay out of the repo, and this file is tracked.

phases.name: Fleet config
phases.validation: `bun run pifleet config validate` exits 0 with ok:. This is the POST-MERGE validation ISC-402 exists for, not a parse -- it enumerated all 9 roles and 16 workers, so the worker -> role -> defaults merge actually ran. config.ts:87 warns in terms that 'parsing is not validating' and that printing ok: for a config `up` then refuses is worse than having no command, so the pyyaml parse I ran first proved only the weak half. Two warnings surfaced (observer pane_mode tui; submit_report beside write on 8 workers) and both are pre-existing and unrelated to gabe.
phases.d7_confirmed_empirically: No worker or role names gabe -- `provider: omlx` appears once and every other model carries an ollama-cloud/ prefix. So the provider is declared and DORMANT: no egress network, no relay, no alias exists for it. That is D7's stated property observed rather than assumed.
phases.reachability_proven: From a container on the fleet host: 401 without the key, 200 with it, against http://192.168.86.199:8001/v1/models. Worth stating precisely -- 6.9.3's earlier 'verified 2026-09-12' can only have concerned route/host reachability, because before Phase 5 that port was bound to loopback and NO container could have reached it. This is the first proof of the actual endpoint from where the fleet will dial.
phases.note: edits fleet.yaml (UNTRACKED, .gitignore:9) so this change CANNOT be carried by a branch, PR or CI run. That is the single biggest reason this SRD was never engineer-shaped work.
phases.what_landed: gabe added as a third sibling in llm.providers after ollama-cloud's probe_timeout_ms (line 360), plus the {host: 192.168.86.199, port: 8001} entry as the FIRST rule in egress.allow -- the second of the two places D9 requires the operator to write the target.
phases.deliberate_omissions: No tag_style (not a tag-style catalogue). No probe_timeout_ms (the fleet-wide 60s is generous for a server that answered a tool-call probe in 2.45s under 8-way concurrency).
phases.allowlist_decision: ONE model, not three. The server serves three NAMES but they are aliases for one set of weights. gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-nvfp4 is now an inherited lie -- it names a quantization that is no longer loaded -- and gemma-4-e4b-it-mxfp8 is LightRAG's dial string. An allowlist entry is a PERMISSION, so permitting a stale alias invites a role to name it.
phases.context_window_reasoning: 32768 is what THIS server was started with. Two other numbers exist and both are wrong here: the checkpoint declares max_position_embeddings 262144, and omlx's bf16 build reports 256000. Undeclared, Pi registers its own 128,000 default.
phases.still_owed: The DHCP reservation. Both base_url and the egress.allow entry are pinned to 192.168.86.199, and a lease move breaks them together.
phases.roles_NOT_assigned: No worker or role names gabe yet. Under D7 nothing is created until a worker resolves to it -- no egress network, no relay, no alias. Assigning seats is a separate operator decision and was deliberately not taken.

PRE_EXISTING_FAULT_FOUND_2026_09_12.what: vllm-metrics-proxy has been serving /metrics/llm and /metrics/emb as dead since roughly 2026-08-15. NOT caused by this rollout -- recorded BEFORE Phase 3 so it cannot later read as collateral from the restart.
PRE_EXISTING_FAULT_FOUND_2026_09_12.mechanism: HostConfig.NetworkMode is `ragnet` but NetworkSettings.Networks is {} -- the container believes it is on ragnet and is attached to NOTHING. Docker's embedded DNS at 127.0.0.11 only exists for containers on a user-defined network, so with zero attachments the resolver is absent.
evidence: getent hosts rag-llm inside the container -> empty
GET /healthz -> 200 (pure nginx, no upstream needed); GET /metrics/llm -> 499
nginx error log: recv() failed (111: Connection refused) while resolving, resolver: 127.0.0.11:53
State.StartedAt 2026-08-15T22:51:04Z with RestartCount 0 -- dark for ~4 weeks
PRE_EXISTING_FAULT_FOUND_2026_09_12.irony_worth_keeping: nginx.conf's own comment documents this exact class of failure already happening once: 'this stranded /metrics/llm after rag-llm was recreated, blanking every generation panel on the dashboard'. The fix built for it -- `resolver 127.0.0.11 valid=10s` plus variable proxy_pass, which re-resolves per request -- is correct and WOULD have survived Phase 3's recreation. It cannot fire because the container has no network to resolve on. The defence is sound; its precondition is missing.
PRE_EXISTING_FAULT_FOUND_2026_09_12.consequence_for_phase_3: NONE. Because the variable proxy_pass form re-resolves per request, recreating rag-llm does not strand this proxy. The metrics path is already down for an unrelated reason and Phase 3 neither worsens nor fixes it.
PRE_EXISTING_FAULT_FOUND_2026_09_12.suggested_repair_NOT_YET_DONE: docker network connect ragnet vllm-metrics-proxy -- one command, no restart, no downtime. Deliberately NOT run: it is outside the authorized phase set and touches a production container. Needs its own decision.
PRE_EXISTING_FAULT_FOUND_2026_09_12.second_issue: Its port binding is 100.126.91.107:9401 -- the Tailscale address. The fleet host is not on Tailscale, so even once repaired this endpoint is unreachable from the fleet.
